messages.text: Man City inquiry moves to appeal stage amid reports majority of PL charges 'proven'

metadata.summary: An independent tribunal has reached decisions in Manchester City's 115 charges case, according to reports.
metadata.content: Man City Premier League charges: Inquiry moves to appeal stage amid reports majority of charges 'proven' | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Breaking Man City Premier League charges: Inquiry moves to appeal stage amid reports majority of charges 'proven' Friday 25 September 2026 16:14, UK An independent tribunal has reached decisions in Manchester City's 115 charges case, according to reports. The reports claim that most of the charges were found to have been proven. Sky Sports News understands that the process is moving to the appeal stage. The Premier League is not commenting as this is a private and confidential process. They will not be providing any guidance. A Manchester City spokesperson said: "The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality. As such Manchester City FC's position remains consistent with the club's statement of February 2023. "The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League Board and Executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence." messages.text: Verstappen usurps Russell in error-filled final practice

metadata.summary: Max Verstappen denied George Russell a clean sweep of fastest practice times as Red Bull led a renewed challenge to the Mercedes drivers ahead of Qualifying later on Friday at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.
metadata.content: Azerbaijan GP: Max Verstappen fastest in challenging final practice to usurp George Russell and Mercedes ahead of Qualifying | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Azerbaijan GP: Max Verstappen fastest in challenging final practice to usurp George Russell and Mercedes ahead of Qualifying Max Verstappen's pace suggests he could vie for Red Bull's first pole position of 2026; George Russell second, Lewis Hamilton third; watch Qualifying later on Friday at 1pm with the Azerbaijan Grand Prix itself on Saturday at 12pm, live on Sky Sports F1 and Main Event Friday 25 September 2026 13:09, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell narrowly avoids hitting wall during the final practice session at the Azerbaijan GP. Max Verstappen denied George Russell a clean sweep of fastest practice times as Red Bull led a renewed challenge to the Mercedes drivers ahead of Qualifying later on Friday at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix. The arrival of more characteristic gusty conditions on the streets of Baku for final practice increased the challenge around the wall-lined circuit, with numerous drivers running off track after errors throughout the hour. Mercedes' dominance from Thursday's calmer running initially continued, but Verstappen found increasing pace on the soft tyres and eventually usurped Russell at the top of the timesheet with a best lap of 1:43.922. Christian Horner says a "dream" role at Ferrari is the only Formula 1 job that could tempt him back onto the pit wall without an ownership stake. Horner was relieved of his dual roles as Red Bull team principal and chief executive following the British Grand Prix in July 2025, ending a hugely successful 20-year stint running the Milton Keynes squad. Having seen out a period following his Red Bull departure during which he was unable to take up work with other teams, Horner has been exploring possible routes back into F1, with his preferred option being to acquire equity of a team. messages.text: Chelsea in landmark fertility policy: 'Being a player and mum are both possible now'

metadata.summary: Chelsea are used to being the first. While plenty of that has come on the pitch, it is the behind the scenes work that is truly leading the way for female players and women's health.
metadata.content: Chelsea Women: Sonia Bompastor and Carly Telford discuss new fertility and player maternity policies in WSL first | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Exclusive Chelsea Women: Sonia Bompastor and Carly Telford discuss new fertility and player maternity policies in WSL first Chelsea are the first team in the WSL to introduce fertility and Player Maternity policies; it gives players the choice to have a family in whichever way they want to, with support during and after starting a family; Sonia Bompastor and Carly Telford explain more to Sky Sports Charlotte Marsh Senior Football Journalist Thursday 24 September 2026 16:28, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Chelsea have introduced fertility and player maternity policies which provide fully paid leave, personalised pregnancy support and dedicated return to play medical care Chelsea are used to being the first. While plenty of that has come on the pitch, it is the behind the scenes work that is truly leading the way for female players and women's health. Now, the Blues are the first team in the WSL to introduced new fertility and maternity policies, giving their players the choice to start a family in whichever way they want to, and the post-natal support to balance the demands of elite sport and motherhood.
